root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service called by frontend, recommendation and checkout, responds with ~10s p50/p99 latency while all peer leaf services respond in ~2ms. Normal CPU, flat memory and zero restarts indicate an injected latency fault rather than resource saturation or a crash.

evidence.observed_value: 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=149092ms (trace 163167d090e59c23 user_get_recommendations 16602ms, trace e6d712832358ded4 user_browse_product 12584ms)

evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU saturation; pod CPU flat during window
error_rate < 0.01 — confirms latency, not error/abort fault

root_causes.description: recommendation calls the slow product-catalog service and inherits its latency (p50 ~5s, p99 10s). It is a victim of upstream latency propagation rather than the origin of the fault.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 < 10ms for a healthy recommendation service

evidence.observed_value: 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=23334ms (trace 1da4c20736cd7b10 user_get_recommendations 22050ms, trace 5316a06ecc8c91eb 16087ms, status ok)

root_causes.description: checkout depends on product-catalog and shows an anomalous p99 spike to 10000ms with a low p50, consistent with intermittent blocking on the slow product-catalog dependency propagating to the frontend.

remediation_steps: Restart / roll the product-catalog deployment to clear any injected latency fault and restore sub-5ms p99 responses.
Inspect flagd feature-flag configuration for a product-catalog latency/failure flag and disable it if set.
Verify the product-catalog pod's network path (sidecar/DNS/egress) for added delay, since CPU/memory/restarts are all nominal.
Add a latency SLO alert on product-catalog server-span p99 to catch leaf-service slowness before it propagates to checkout/recommendation/frontend.
Temporarily scale product-catalog replicas to absorb request queuing while the latency fault is mitigated.
